It solves the problem of high memory consumption in standard sparse volumes by replacing stored values with trained neural networks, enabling high-resolution storage and random access while maintaining compatibility with existing VDB pipelines [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that NeuralVDB solves high memory consumption by replacing stored values with trained neural networks, enabling high-resolution storage and random access while maintaining compatibility with existing VDB pipelines. The evidence supports this in multiple ways: 1) It explicitly mentions using neural representations for values (and optionally tree structure) to achieve high-fidelity reconstruction while consuming much less memory than compressed VDB. 2) It states that NeuralVDB is compatible with existing VDB pipelines by design. 3) It describes variants optimized for fast random access (e.g., [Hash, 5, 4, NN(3)]) and demonstrates its use in run-time applications like ray-marching. 4) It explains the mechanism of replacing explicit values with MLPs (neural networks) that map coordinates to values.
